title: gpro-jisatsu-championship
label: "Demon Boy" Ishrinku

won.source: Won a five-man scaffold battle royal, "Rumble in the Sky," on Mini-supercard (12 September 1998, Kawasaki Arena).

note: Successfully defended the title against Keiji Asamiya and Ghost Warrior Rudiger in a three-way at Blast-Off (29 September 1998, Osaka Dome), then lost it to Bram Black at Luchamania '98 in a tables match that required an eleventh table when the first ten weren't enough to produce a winner.

lost.source: Lost the title to Bram Black in a tables match at Luchamania '98.

title: gpro-super-middleweight-championship
label: Kashan Akuma

won.source: Won the Super-Middleweight Title tournament final against The Banshee at Blast-Off (29 September 1998, Osaka Dome).

note: Lost to Shoji Suzuki at El Dias de los Muertos in a three-way unification match that also involved the Tijuana Lucha Lightweight Championship.

lost.source: Lost the title to Shoji Suzuki at El Dias de los Muertos.

title: gpro-asia-pacific-heavyweight-championship
label: Frazer Fury

won.source: Won the Heavyweight Title tournament final against Jason Storm at Blast-Off (29 September 1998, Osaka Dome); the ring announcer names Fury explicitly as the winner.

note: Stripped after a storyline disappearance; the vacancy was filled two weeks later by a four-way match at El Dias de los Muertos that unified this title with two Tijuana Lucha titles into the new G-Pro Triple Crown, won there by Jason Storm.

lost.source: Stripped by Commissioner Oyadama on Battlefield after failing to appear for a scheduled title defense against Ozeki Shumasita; the vacant title was unified into the new G-Pro Triple Crown two weeks later.

title: gpro-trios-championship
label: Zokugun Sangai

won.source: Won a twelve-man, four-team cage elimination match, "Caged Chaos," on Mini-supercard (12 September 1998, Kawasaki Arena), fielding Frazer Fury, Kashan Akuma and a last-minute-substitute TORA Wanizame.

note: Lost to the Daimyo on Battlefield (3 October 1998); the title passed from the Daimyo to Hiryuu Batsu on 15 November 1998.

lost.source: Lost the title to the Daimyo on Battlefield.

title: gpro-jisatsu-championship
label: Bram Black

won.source: Put "Demon Boy" Ishrinku through the sixth and final table with a top-rope double underhook powerbomb in a tables match at Luchamania '98, after officials ordered an eleventh table brought out when the first ten weren't enough to decide the match.

note: Won the title from "Demon Boy" Ishrinku at Luchamania '98; survived a non-title challenge from a touring rival on the following Battlefield (11 January 1999).

title: gpro-triple-crown-championship
label: Jason Storm

won.source: Won a four-way unification match at El Dias de los Muertos against Ozeki Shumasita, Cuervo (the Tijuana Lucha Heavyweight Champion) and Fuego Tigre Jr (the Tijuana Lucha Middleweight Champion), eliminating Fuego Tigre Jr by submission and Cuervo by pinfall before pinning Shumasita last with a backdrop driver.

note: The title was created that night by unifying the vacant Asia Pacific Heavyweight Championship with two Tijuana Lucha titles. Survived a later challenge from the promotion's own Jisatsu champion in a non-title cage match at Luchamania '98, and a still later challenge from the promotion's own Jisatsu champion in his first defense of 1999; a rival wrestler aired audio afterward alleging the champion's own manager interfered in that finish.

title: gpro-combative-tag-team-championship
label: TORA Wanizame and Jason Storm

won.source: Won the tournament final against "Demon Boy" Ishrinku and The Banshee on Battlefield, the promotion's own first-ever Combative Tag Team title tournament having run across three broadcasts.

note: The inaugural Combative Tag Team Champions; no document in this reading dates the title's own passage to the Fabulous Ones, who are separately attested holding it by February 1999 and who describe it on that broadcast as a newly created division, an in-fiction framing the held record does not bear out.

title: gpro-trios-championship
label: The Daimyo

won.source: Won the trios title from Zokugun Sangai on Battlefield when Sho Satsuma pinned Frazer Fury after a low blow from Jack Banks went unseen by the referee.

lost.source: Lost the title to Hiryuu Batsu on Battlefield.

note: Successfully defended between these dates in matches this reading did not read in full.

title: gpro-trios-championship
label: Hiryuu Batsu

won.source: Won the trios title from the Daimyo on Battlefield when Shoji Suzuki pinned Sho Satsuma with a fisherman buster, the promotion's own Combative Tag Team title tournament final airing on the same broadcast.

note: Successfully defended against Zokugun Sangai at Luchamania '98 (6 December 1998) in a match where every man's own singles title was also on the line; the trio won two falls to one, the deciding pinfall also making The Banshee the new International Super-Middleweight Champion.

title: gpro-super-middleweight-championship
label: Shoji Suzuki

won.source: Pinned Kashan Akuma with the Jaguar Special in a three-way unification match against Akuma and Crotalo Negro (the Tijuana Lucha Lightweight Champion) at El Dias de los Muertos.

lost.source: Pinned by TORA Wanizame in the International Trios title match at Luchamania '98, where every man's own singles title was also on the line.

note: The Jaguar Special, his finisher named for his own tag alias Jet Jaguar, won him the title.

title: gpro-super-middleweight-championship
label: TORA Wanizame

won.source: Pinned Shoji Suzuki with a Tiger Driver '91 in the International Trios title match at Luchamania '98, where every man's own singles title was also on the line.

lost.source: Pinned by The Banshee moments later in the same match, the deciding fall also handing Hiryuu Batsu the Trios title.

note: Held the title for a matter of seconds inside the same bout that won it; the broadcast's own commentary makes a joke of the reign's length.

won.source: Rolled up TORA Wanizame for the deciding pinfall of the International Trios title match at Luchamania '98, where every man's own singles title was also on the line.

title: gpro-combative-tag-team-championship
label: The Fabulous Ones

won.source: The promotion's own billing on its 5 February 1999 newsletter, in which the champions themselves announce the win on camera; no surviving document in the held record dates or details the title's own first tournament or match.

note: The champions frame the title as newly created for the promotion's own tag division, but this reading finds an earlier reign: TORA Wanizame and Jason Storm won the actual inaugural Combative Tag Team title in a tournament final on Battlefield (15 November 1998); no document in the held record dates the title's later passage to the Fabulous Ones.
